children: The Brand Leadership Showcase – Hyatt moved into a one-on-one conversation with Vikas Chawla, President, India & Southwest Asia, Hyatt

The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme
‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’
, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.
The
Brand Leadership Showcase – Hyatt

moved into a one-on-one conversation on the changing dynamics of Indian hospitality, bringing together two experienced industry voices to reflect on the market, its growth trajectory and what lies ahead.
Rattan Keswani, Former Deputy MD, Lemon Tree Hotels
, was in conversation with
Vikas Chawla, President, India & Southwest Asia, Hyatt
. The exchange touched on Hyatt’s presence in India, the evolution of the hospitality market and the opportunities emerging for the sector.

“I am very passionate about growth. I have always had that hunger for growth, and that is something that has stayed with me throughout my journey. I think there is always an opportunity to do more, to learn more and to build something bigger,” said Chawla.

“Hyatt has a very special place in my heart. I have never seen a brand where the culture is breathed by every single person. It is not just something that is written down or spoken about; you can actually see it in the way people work, interact and lead,” he said.

“I never had plans for doing hospitality. It was not something that I had originally planned as a career. But hospitality has such a welcoming vibe, and over time, I realised how much I enjoyed being part of this industry and the people within it,” he said.

“Hyatt has a very special place in my heart. I have never seen a brand where the culture is breathed by every single person. It is not just something that is written down or spoken about; you can actually see it in the way people work, interact and lead,” he noted.

“Culture starts from the top. When you have the culture at the top, the leaders pass on the same essence to the team. It becomes something that moves through the organisation, from the leadership to the teams and ultimately to the way we deliver the business,” Chawla said. “We want to grow, and we want to grow much more over the next five to seven years. We have a good foundation today, and we would like to be five times what we are today. That is the ambition, and I think the opportunity in India gives us the confidence to think about that kind of growth,” he said.

“If we happen to fall short, it would be because of the crunch of talent in the industry. The opportunity is very large, but for us to capture that opportunity, we need to make sure that we have the right people, the right leaders and the right talent to support that growth,” he said.  As the conversation drew to a close, the focus remained squarely on Hyatt's strategic positioning in a rapidly evolving market. By balancing global brand standards with tailored local experiences, Hyatt demonstrated how deepening owner relationships and targeting high-growth leisure and urban markets will drive its long-term market presence."

Rattan Keswani, Former Deputy MD, Lemon Tree Hotels, warmly welcomed Vikas Chawla, President, India & Southwest Asia, Hyatt, to the IHA 2026 stage. The conversation brought together two prominent voices from the hospitality industry to discuss the sector’s growth, evolving talent landscape and the opportunities shaping its next phase.

As the conversation drew to a close, the focus remained squarely on Hyatt's strategic positioning in a rapidly evolving market. By balancing global brand standards with tailored local experiences, Hyatt demonstrated how deepening owner relationships and targeting high-growth leisure and urban markets will drive its long-term market presence.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
